pos.personaBrief: Inzaghi's teams have at least equal possession but do not chase domination, use mid/low blocks and vertical transitions (Coaches' Voice, Spielverlagerung), and Delaney calls Inter reactive.

pro.personaBrief: Short build-up through the thirds but always forward and penetrating as a priority, with fast wing-back runs after a trigger pass (Coaches' Voice, Spielverlagerung).

est.personaBrief: Rotations and fluid vertical movement (Immobile blind-side runs, centre-back stepping into midfield) inside a fixed 3-5-2 with wing-backs holding the width.

lar.personaBrief: Most crosses in Serie A in 2022/23 and 2023/24, wing-backs exploiting width; 3-5-2 with no wingers and two central strikers.

blo.personaBrief: A 5-3-2 mid/low block with a wide pressing trap, more mid-block at Inter; forwards still press the keeper (Laziali) but no relentless high press.

mar.personaBrief: Single match evidence of a mix of man and zonal marking at set pieces; the block is space-based with a 5-man line.

pla.personaBrief: Almost exclusively the same 3-5-2 at both clubs, with in-game adjustments such as the Lazzari for Jony switch; called reactive but not abandoning his model.

res.personaBrief: Pragmatic winner of trophies with solid defensive structure, more concerned with results than aesthetics; reactive in games.

sis.personaBrief: Drilled 3-5-2 system with defined roles and heavy rotation of key players, though he gave players more freedom than Conte.

jog.personaBrief: Technically capable build-up players (Lucas Leiva, Acerbi as deep midfielder, Milinkovic-Savic) valued over pure physical duels.

bas.personaBrief: Won titles with an experienced core at Inter and rotated veterans; squad depth was relied upon more than academy graduates.

lid.personaBrief: Calm man-manager who rotates and rests players and gave more tactical freedom than Conte, but remains the final decision-maker.
